NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md: current authority and browser/source corrections
TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md: current authoring and verification workflow
evidence: Reviewed all 31 criteria (3 gates, 23 Functional, 2 Polish, 3 Visual). One non-outcome bar remains: task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 requires a custom DOM/canvas/SVG surface, excludes "another ready-made editor implementing the document surface", asks the judge to use "browser-loaded asset evidence" and "explain how the surface actually handles editing", and hard-fails the entire gate for provenance regardless of observed ability. task/tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md:7 explicitly permits reading loaded assets to identify implementation ownership. The public requirement is task/environment/instructions/ui.md:3 ("your own DOM, canvas or SVG text model"). DOM inspection can decide the narrower textarea/input/contenteditable document-surface restriction, but rendered editing, loaded asset labels and functional actions cannot decide whether an otherwise identical custom-looking text model was authored by this participant or supplied as an unfamiliar ready-made editor. No browser-visible distinguishing experiment or reliable bounded provenance classifier is specified. Workbook Quality/Internal row 33 and skill quality-checks.md:134-136 demand concrete browser outcomes and identify a source read as a defect; REVIEW_POLICY.md states browser exchanges cannot prove task-added implementation mandates. The remaining criteria use real edit/run/state transitions, exact source/selection readbacks, computed visible styles, independently fetched saved revisions, restart observations, or anchored screenshot judgments. The two verified golden log hashes provide useful scripted examples of these concrete observations, but their DIV/editable=false/codemirror=false surface evidence cannot establish the broader ownership/provenance claim. These logs are not a configured judge or actual MCP completion measurement.
counterexample: A prohibited unfamiliar ready-made DOM or canvas editor can be vendored into the frontend bundle, with package metadata and class names stripped, and expose the same rendered source, real caret/selection/undo behavior and loaded assets as an independently written text model. It passes every distinguishing browser action and the observable surface checks while violating the "your own"/no-ready-made mandate. Conversely, an independently written custom text model can use the same rendering structures and generic algorithmic patterns as a library; inferring ready-made provenance from those similarities would hard-zero a conforming app. Identical browser bytes and behavior cannot distinguish the implementation provenance of these cases.
suggested_fix: Remove the task-added own-implementation/no-ready-made provenance bar from the public notes and gate; retain the concrete inspectable document-surface restrictions and score the existing custom-editor behavior probes. If provenance is essential, resolve the browser-only evaluation contract explicitly rather than treating loaded-source inference as an observed product outcome.
